newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - World Bank wows with pesos.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - World Bank wows with pesos.

text.p: The World Bank on Thursday wowed the Asian debt markets with a Philippine peso bond, the second launched this week.
The World Bank this morning launched the 2.75 billion Philippine peso ($104.5 million) Eurobond. It has a five-year maturity and offers a 10.25 percent coupon.
It was priced during London hours at 101.414 and re-offered at 100.04. At the same time, it was increased to 3.0 billion pesos. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was the lead.
The World Bank bond comes on the heels of an almost identical issue launched on Monday by the International Finance Corp (IFC), the World Bank's investment arm.

The IFC bond attracted both institutional and retail investors, according to lead manager Citicorp International. About 70 percent of the bond placed in Asia, with about 25 percent going to the U.S. and the remainder to Europe.
In other news, the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) plans to launch the first issue of its recently signed US$500 million medium-term note programme shortly, bankers said.
The US$100 million step-up subordinated note issue will be lead managed by SBC Warburg and Citibank International. Launch is expected as early as today.
The notes have a final maturity of 10 years but can be called after five.

The notes are expected to pay a margin of between 75 and 90 basis points over the London Interbank Offered (LIBOR) rate for the first five years and 185-200 basis points over LIBOR for years six to 10 if the notes are not called.

Representatives from India's financial regulatory bodies were in Hong Kong today as part of a roadshow to highlight recent reforms in India's financial markets, including the opening up of the local debt market to foreign investors.

Speaking at the Merrill Lynch conference, Narendra Jadhav, officer-in-charge in the Reserve Bank of India's Department of Economics, said India currently has no plans to launch a sovereign bond but may in the future as the country's external balances improve.
Many bankers have suggested that India should launch a sovereign bond to create an international benchmark.
